subject: zoology
question_text: Name the type of caudal fin and scales that are present in a shark and Catla, respectively.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.55, VSAQ 110). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK WORDING: the book answers 'scales are cycloid or ctenoid' for Catla. Catla catla is a carp and carries CYCLOID scales; ctenoid scales are found in perch-like bony fishes. The card writes cycloid.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Shark
steps.margin_note: Name the group, then the fin, then the scale. Three short lines.
lines: Its caudal fin is heterocercal: the upper lobe
is longer than the lower lobe.
steps.why: A shark is cartilaginous and a Catla is bony, so naming the group first makes both answers follow from one fact instead of two memorised pairs.
common_mistakes: Writing homocercal for the shark. The two lobes of a shark tail are unequal.
Giving cycloid scales to the shark. Placoid scales belong to cartilaginous fishes.
steps.memory_tip: Hetero means unequal: the shark tail has unequal lobes.

steps.label: Catla
steps.margin_note: One boxed line answers the whole question; the rest is the reason.
lines: Its caudal fin is homocercal: the two lobes
steps.why: Homo means equal, so the word itself tells the shape of the tail and there is nothing extra to remember.
common_mistakes: Writing placoid for Catla. Placoid scales are found only in cartilaginous fishes.
Leaving out one half of the answer. Each fish needs both the fin and the scale.
steps.memory_tip: Cartilaginous shark: unequal tail, placoid. Bony Catla: equal tail, cycloid.

insider_note: Four words carry the two marks — heterocercal, placoid, homocercal, cycloid — so write all four even if you write nothing else.
